name: Philippines

findings.summary: At a September 2020 Senate hearing Globe's counsel said roughly 80% of its network equipment came from Huawei, the rest Ericsson and Nokia, and that the board had begun talks on replacing Huawei gear.
findings.analyst_inference: Single S3 source from 2020. Globe stated an intent to move to non-Chinese vendors; no evidence found in this pass that a replacement was executed, so the Huawei installed base is coded as the current state and no reversal is coded.

findings.summary: PLDT and its mobile arm Smart selected Ericsson to deploy 5G-ready network equipment in 2018.
findings.analyst_inference: Sources seen in search results only (titles); contract value not established. Ericsson is Swedish, hence pole third. Search results also showed 2019 reporting of Huawei competing for PLDT 5G work; PLDT's full vendor mix was not resolved.

findings.summary: Trade press reported Huawei and ZTE as DITO's prime network vendors, with ZTE affiliate Whale Cloud supplying BSS/OSS; DITO is 40% owned by state-owned China Telecom.
findings.analyst_inference: Supply deals were not publicly announced by DITO per the source; single S2 source, so uncorroborated.

findings.summary: The AFP signed a memorandum of agreement letting DITO, part-owned by China Telecom, place cell towers and equipment on military bases; it drew Senate calls for security review.
findings.analyst_inference: BenarNews is US-government-funded, so treated as S4. Pole prc reflects China Telecom's minority stake and vendor mix; DITO's controlling shareholders are Philippine (Udenna/Chelsea), so control is mixed. MOA coded as tier 2 framework access.

findings.summary: PLDT's data-centre arm VITRO runs a 50 MW AI-ready hyperscale site in Sta. Rosa, Laguna, operating since July 2024 and inaugurated April 2025, with plans for up to 500 MW.
findings.analyst_inference: PLDT is Philippine-incorporated, hence domestic, though it has significant foreign shareholders; investment value undisclosed.

findings.summary: VITRO Sta. Rosa hosts Nvidia-powered GPU servers and sells GPU-as-a-service to enterprise and government customers.
findings.analyst_inference: GPU count and model are undisclosed, so 'at scale' is unverified; tier 5 reflects operational deployment rather than a known fleet size. Date is the site's operational start, not a confirmed GPU go-live date.

findings.local_actor: STT GDC Philippines (JV with Globe Telecom and Ayala Corp.)
findings.summary: STT GDC Philippines is building STT Fairview 1 in Quezon City, a 124 MW-design campus; in late 2024 phase 1 was reported on track for service by Q2 2025.
findings.analyst_inference: Ownership percentages undisclosed; pole third assumes the Singapore-headquartered operator controls operations, with Globe and Ayala as local partners. Whether phase 1 actually opened was not confirmed in this pass. Malaya page date unreliable.

findings.local_actor: Department of Information and Communications Technology
findings.summary: DICT and Google Cloud announced an expanded multi-year collaboration giving 50,000 civil servants Gemini Enterprise, rising to 200,000+ within 18 months, plus Gemini-based agents for e-government.
findings.analyst_inference: Instrument type not stated in sources (no contract or value disclosed), so coded tier 2 despite an initial rollout; upgrade if a procurement award surfaces. Manila Bulletin seen in search results only.

findings.local_actor: DICT National Security Operations Center; PS-DBM eMarketplace
findings.summary: Same DICT-Google package covers citizen-facing multilingual AI agents on e-government platforms and a Google Cloud cyberdefense alliance centred on the National Security Operations Center.
findings.analyst_inference: Package also references integrating Google-linked TPU and Apricot subsea cables with the DICT Luzon Bypass; not coded separately as networks.

findings.controller: China International Telecommunication Construction Corp. (Huawei equipment reported)
findings.local_actor: Department of the Interior and Local Government
findings.summary: DILG signed a P20-billion Safe Philippines contract with state-owned CITCC for 12,000 CCTV cameras in Metro Manila and Davao plus a command centre with facial recognition, to be financed by a Chinese loan.
findings.analyst_inference: Approx. USD value not converted. Huawei's equipment role was reported by Inquirer but not confirmed by officials per Philstar. Both sources S3, so uncorroborated under the S1/S2 rule.

findings.controller: China International Telecommunication Construction Corp. / China Eximbank
findings.local_actor: Department of the Interior and Local Government
findings.reversal_of: PHL-010 Safe Philippines CCTV contract with CITCC (2018)
findings.summary: DILG recommended cancelling the Safe Philippines CCTV project in late 2021 after China Eximbank loan funds were never released; it was shelved, though officials floated a revival with new bidders in 2022.
findings.analyst_inference: Status after May 2022 not checked; a revival under new bidders would not restore the PRC finding unless a PRC contractor won again.

power.null_reason: search budget spent on higher-priority layers; no AI-specific power evidence surfaced incidentally

research_gaps: Did Globe actually replace its Huawei RAN/core after the 2020 stated intent? Current vendor share?
Current PLDT/Smart and DITO 5G vendor mix (Huawei/ZTE vs Ericsson/Nokia) as of 2025-2026.
Was the Safe Philippines CCTV project revived after 2022, and with which contractor?
Did STT Fairview 1 phase 1 enter service in 2025?
Instrument type and value of the 2026 DICT-Google Cloud deal (procurement award or MOU?).
Nvidia GPU fleet size at VITRO Sta. Rosa; any other large accelerator deployments.
PRC-built (HMN Tech) submarine cable landings in the Philippines - not searched.
Whether the AFP-DITO military-base MOA was later revised or suspended.
